_meta: Topic queue — the human-controlled INPUT to the content engine. Topics come from real Tricity demand, never invented by the model. The engine pulls the first status:"pending" entry per run, processes exactly one, and writes the outcome back here. This file is the audit trail / proof of editorial oversight. Statuses: pending | published | skipped-dup | killed-commodity | halted-factcheck.

title: Petrol scooter vs low-speed EV in the Tricity: the real one-year cost, in rupees
imagePrompt: A petrol scooter and an electric scooter parked side by side on a clean tree-lined Chandigarh sector road, modernist concrete architecture in the background
angle: Work the actual year-one running cost on Chandigarh's cheap domestic tariff (Rs 2.80-3.75/unit) against a 100cc petrol commuter — the local power price is the ownable hook a generic petrol-vs-EV answer can't have.

title: Buying your first electric scooter in the Tricity: a plain decision guide
imagePrompt: A first-time rider standing beside a low-speed electric scooter on a calm Chandigarh sector street, daytime
angle: A decision framework keyed to daily distance and the no-licence (<=25 km/h, <=250W) exemption — route the reader to match commute km to battery type, not to a specific model.

title: Charging a low-speed EV without a garage: options for Tricity flats
imagePrompt: A removable electric-scooter battery being carried up to a Chandigarh apartment for charging from a regular wall socket
angle: Practical charging for apartment and rented-accommodation riders with no private parking — removable batteries, a regular 5A/15A socket, and the ~1.5-2 units per full charge. Distinct from the home-charging-cost page: this is the 'where do I plug in' problem, not the 'what does it cost' one.

title: Why your EV scooter's real range is less than the brochure (and how to plan for it)
imagePrompt: An electric scooter's handlebar display showing battery level, on a Chandigarh road with sector greenery
angle: Explain the gap between claimed and real-world range honestly (rider weight, terrain, battery type, age) and tie it to typical Tricity commute distances so a buyer sizes the battery for the route they actually ride.

title: Lead-acid or lithium for your low-speed scooter? Match the battery to your daily km
imagePrompt: Two electric-scooter batteries side by side, a heavier lead-acid pack and a lighter lithium-ion pack, on a clean workshop bench
angle: Honest total-cost-over-life comparison: lead-acid's lower sticker vs lithium's lighter weight, faster charge and longer life. Use the data layer's guidance (above ~60 km/day, choose lithium) as the deciding line.

title: A low-speed electric scooter for seniors in the Tricity: no licence, ride today
imagePrompt: A senior citizen comfortably seated on a low-speed electric scooter with a low seat height, on a quiet Chandigarh sector lane
angle: Why the no-licence, low-seat, gearless low-speed class suits older riders for short local trips — framed on ease and the ready-to-ride exemption, not on selling a particular scooter.

title: Do you need insurance for a no-RTO electric scooter in Chandigarh, Mohali or Panchkula?
imagePrompt: A low-speed electric scooter parked near a Tricity insurance/RTO office signage context, clean daylight
angle: Walk the genuinely grey area honestly: insurance is not legally mandated for an exempt low-speed scooter, interpretations differ, and enforcement varies across the UT, Punjab and Haryana — so the answer is 'confirm with your local RTO', not a flat yes/no.

title: Keeping a low-speed electric scooter healthy through a Tricity monsoon and summer
imagePrompt: A low-speed electric scooter parked under shelter during light Chandigarh monsoon rain, wet sector road
angle: Seasonal ownership advice specific to the Tricity climate — wet-season riding and storage, summer heat and battery care — practical local guidance a generic maintenance answer wouldn't localise.
